title: Book One · Chapter 114: Mr Qiu Has His Own List
story:
Mr Qiu sits at Mum's table with his own small notebook.

He comes to check the dry crates and speak to Mrs Lan. Mrs Lan is talking to a neighbour. Mr Qiu waits until she is free. Mum offers him tea, but still has work to do.

Ronan watches him draw two lines on the page.

“Is that a new map?”

“No. Things I need to do.”

“Fix the roof.”

“Ask about the roof. I do not fix roofs.”

“Open the stall.”

“Find somewhere suitable to sell. I need that while someone repairs the roof.”

“Here?” Ronan asks at once.

Mr Qiu closes the notebook a little. “Mrs Lan agreed to store my boxes. I have not asked her for a place to sell.”

“Could you ask now?”

“I will speak to her. She can say no.”

Ronan looks at the green gate. He imagines Mr Qiu here every day. In this plan, Mr Qiu is safe. Ronan can see him every day. But Mrs Lan must use the gate too. How will she carry her washing bowl past customers? He did not think about that before.

“Is the road outside busy at school time?” Mr Qiu asks. Ronan tells him about the carts. Mum adds some important times. The gate must stay clear at those times. This is useful information. It is not yet permission.

Leo comes to borrow Ronan's yellow ruler. He asked to borrow it first. Then he came over. He promises to bring it back the next morning. He sees Mr Qiu. “Did you lose all your stock?” he asks.

“Most is dry,” Mr Qiu says. “Some paper is damaged. Six books are drying at school.”

“My mother thought the whole stall fell down.”

“The roof leaks. The stall has not fallen down.”

Leo looks embarrassed. “I will tell her.”

“Thank you.”

Ronan wants to make a clear notice. “The whole stall fell down,” people say. A notice can tell them the true facts. He fetches a clean sheet of his birthday paper.

“What shall I write?”

Mr Qiu thinks. “Closed for roof work. Ask me about reopening. First we need a place for the notice. Then we can put it up.”

Ronan writes the first line in pencil. He draws the stall below it. It is a small shape, with a low shelf and the little cup of rulers.

Mr Qiu smiles at the cup. “Your picture looks very tidy.”

“It can be tidy.”

“For five minutes.”

They laugh. Then Mrs Lan comes to the door. She asks to speak with Mr Qiu privately. Ronan gathers his paper. He does not stay to listen through the wall.

In the yard, Leo asks, “Will we be famous? Are we saving the stall?” “We did not save the stall,” Ronan says. “We made number labels. We helped with books.”

“That does not sound like a great story,” Leo says.

Ronan looks at his drawing. Can he write an exciting story? He thinks about this. He looks at the empty space under his drawing.

After Leo leaves, Mum asks him to put away the ruler's cloth cover until the ruler comes back. She wants the table clear. He folds it and puts it beside his tin.

Mr Qiu leaves. There is no new selling agreement. Mrs Lan wants to think about her room first. She has more questions about the space. The rain begins again before he reaches the corner. Ronan watches his umbrella until he turns the corner. Then he sits down with the unfinished drawing. His sharp pencil is beside it.
studyGuide:
## 重点表达

- suitable＝合适的
- privately＝私下地
- damaged＝受损的
- reopening＝重新营业

额外情节词（不要求本章全部记住）：notice＝告示；label＝标签；famous＝出名的。

## 读句提示

**Did you lose all your stock?**

你／丢失了／所有存货吗？直接问题后，Qiu马上说明大部分仍干。

## 理解问题

1. MrQiu自己的待办事项与Ronan想象的有什么不同？
2. 哪些未经核实的说法让问题显得更大？
